questions.q: A basement wall sits in groundwater under constant hydrostatic pressure. What protection does it need?
questions.n: Damp-proofing only stops capillary moisture; hydrostatic pressure needs true waterproofing.

questions.q: Negative-side basement waterproofing is applied:
o: On the inside face of the wall
questions.n: Negative side means the face opposite the water pressure, inside.

questions.q: Waterproofing that is mixed into the concrete at batching, rather than applied afterward, is called:
questions.n: Integral admixtures make the concrete itself water-resistant.

questions.q: A planted podium deck has ponding, moving joints, root pressure and will be buried under soil. Which waterproofing system fits best?
questions.n: Bituminous membranes tolerate movement and standing water, and work under backfill with a root barrier.

questions.q: A substance that blocks fluids, dust, sound and air through joints, often the same as caulk, is a:
questions.n: Sealants are applied wet and cure flexible.

questions.q: Which below-grade material seals itself by swelling when it gets wet, filling cracks and joints?
questions.n: Sodium bentonite expands many times on hydration and self-seals.

questions.q: Flexible asphalt-based sheets heat-fused to the deck describe:
questions.n: Torch-on membranes are bituminous sheets fused with a flame.

questions.q: A rigid or semi-rigid waterproofing used where it won't see sun or weather, such as water tanks and basements, is typically:
questions.n: Cementitious systems are common for concealed, non-exposed areas.

questions.q: A 100 mm (4") slab on grade gets sawn control joints. How deep is the cut?
o: About 25 mm (1"), a quarter of the slab
questions.n: The rule is one quarter of the slab thickness, so the crack forms at the cut.

questions.q: Three of these are elastomeric waterproofing products. Which one is the cement-based odd one out?
questions.n: Thoroseal is cementitious; the others are flexible elastomeric products.

questions.q: A joint deliberately left where one day's pour stops and the next begins is a:
questions.n: Construction joints mark planned breaks between pours.

questions.q: A sawed or tooled groove that weakens a slab so it cracks along a planned line is a:
questions.n: Shrinkage cracks follow the groove.

questions.q: A basement on high, well-drained ground with no water table pressure usually just needs:
questions.n: Without hydrostatic pressure, damp-proofing against soil moisture is enough.

questions.q: A damp basement CHB wall needs a brush-on, cement-based coating that bonds into the masonry instead of sitting on top as a film. Which product type is that?
o: A cementitious waterproofing slurry such as Thoroseal
questions.n: Cementitious slurries are brushed onto damp masonry and become part of the substrate.

questions.q: A single-ply synthetic rubber sheet membrane is:
questions.n: EPDM is a single-layer synthetic rubber membrane.

questions.q: A seawall and pier deck must hold up against saltwater. Which waterproofing approach is usually recommended for the concrete itself?
questions.n: Crystalline systems seal the pores of the concrete against chloride-laden water.

questions.q: Which wall has to resist hydrostatic pressure?
questions.n: Groundwater pushes against below-grade walls.

questions.q: Preformed floor expansion joint fillers are most commonly made of:
questions.n: Compressible foam fillers let the slab move.

questions.q: On a large ready-mix slab on grade, what commonly replaces loose rebar as shrinkage reinforcement?
questions.n: Welded wire fabric is quick to lay over large slab areas.

questions.q: Xypex seals concrete by growing crystals in its pores and capillaries. It belongs to which family?
questions.n: Xypex is a crystalline system that self-seals hairline cracks.

questions.q: Sealant backer rods are usually:
questions.n: Closed-cell PE rod controls sealant depth and prevents three-sided bonding.

questions.q: Which is NOT a cementitious waterproofing product?
questions.n: Rain or Shine is an elastomeric paint; the others are cement-based.

questions.q: Slab-on-grade construction joints are commonly filled with:
questions.n: Bituminous filler is the traditional joint filler for slabs on grade.
